content:
sara_sales: Heads-up: NeoPay (EU financial customer) wants a tight POC. Requirements: strict data geofence (all data in EU), KMS BYOK with HSM, and a predictable failover path that never prefers non-EU endpoints. Also asked for an estimate of the incremental cost for warm-standby vs fully multi-region.

alex_presales: Got it. Key questions: do they need control plane pinned too or just data plane? They also want an example attestation showing key locality + subprocessors.

sara_sales: Both control and data pinned to EU required. Control plane in eu-west-1 only. They explicitly said "no control-plane telemetry to US."

carla_solutions: For demos, we can show a pinned tenant in eu-west-1 with a warm standby in eu-north-1. Warm standby would keep minimal reserved capacity and spin up on failover. We should document the sequence: detection -> scale-up -> DNS shift -> session rebind.

mike_infra: Tech note: to guarantee no non-EU egress, configure routing + geofence at the edge and enforce absence of cross-region KV replication that leaks tokens. For near-zero data-loss you'd need synchronous replication which cross-borders; so the tradeoff is either slight RPO or accept intra-EU sync only (eu-west <-> eu-north is intra-EU).

lina_security: Subprocessors: I can provide the list for eu-west-1 and eu-north-1. Auditbot: attaching SOC2/ISO references and a BYOK attestation template.

auditbot: (auto) Attached: SOC2_summary.pdf, ISO27001_summary.pdf, BYOK_attestation_template.docx

emma_ops: Pricing note: typical structure we show: base reserved pool in primary region + warm-standby multiplier (0.2-0.35x) for capacity kept ready. If they want hot-active multi-region it's ~1.7-2.0x. Also add small network egress buffer in estimate if cross-border allowed.

sara_sales: NeoPay asked for binding language for contract: no subprocessor outside EU, data center locality guarantee, and right to audit. Can legal accept our subprocessors list + attestation only or they want specific contractual clauses?

lina_security: Legal prefers adding explicit Data Processing Addendum (DPA) clauses for geo-restriction and BYOK assurances. I'll coordinate with legal. Meanwhile I'll paste the subprocessors snippet here.

lina_security: Subprocessors (eu-only): cloud-hosting-provider-eu, metrics-aggregator-eu, kms-provider-eu (HSM), logging-archive-eu. No third-party devtools agents allowed for EU-only tenants unless customer consents.

mike_infra: Routing policy example we can include in the one-pager (yaml):
```
routing:
  tenant_pin: eu-west-1
  allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-north-1]
  failover:
    mode: warm-standby
    priority: [eu-west-1, eu-north-1]
    allow_non_eu: false
    rto_target_seconds: 300
    rpo_target_seconds: 10
```

carla_solutions: For the demo runbook: 1) confirm tenant pin, 2) inject failover via /ops/failover trigger, 3) monitor replication lag, 4) validate keystore access (BYOK) in EU, 5) smoke test payment flow. I'll draft a 1-page runbook.

emma_ops: Operational caveat: warm-standby warm-up time depends on model cache and KV size. Recommend pre-warming KV index metadata and preloading model shards used by customer's workload.

sara_sales: Action items: Lina -> subprocessors + attestation (today), Alex -> pricing + 1-pager (EOD), Carla -> demo runbook (tomorrow morning), Mike/Emma -> infra/runbook notes for warm-start.

alex_presales: I'll prepare a short quote showing: (a) reserved primary monthly, (b) warm-standby uplift, (c) optional hot-active scenario, plus assumptions about traffic and token volume.

lina_security: Uploading subprocessors list now. Also note: telemetry defaults to EU for pinned tenants; control-plane telemetry to non-EU only if customer enables investigational features.

sara_sales: Thanks. NeoPay wants the one-pager + price ballpark before the Tuesday exec sync. Can we target Monday EOD?

carla_solutions: Monday EOD works for the one-pager. I'll also include a short checklist for the demo environment build.

(reacts: :white_check_mark: by carla_solutions, :rocket: by alex_presales)
